While these intervals account for a wide range of expected fluctuations, certain high-impact risks or events could indeed push outcomes beyond these boundaries. Conversely, a severe economic recession, an unforeseen geopolitical crisis escalating into widespread instability, or aggressive tightening of monetary policy in response to rampant inflation could trigger a sharp downturn, pushing the value below the lower bounds. These types of "black swan" events or extreme shifts in fundamental conditions represent significant deviations from the range of outcomes factored into the probabilistic forecast.
